result: ⛔ THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT MADE THE JOB SMALLER AND THE ANSWER SHARPER. It reads as though the published sets were fetched narrow. They were not: `signature_scores` already scores each set over its FULL readable membership. The narrowing is one file downstream — `ndrg1_panel_attribution.py` re-derives per-sample panel scores from `gene_reads`, which is by construction the union of PANELS' hand-curated groups (479 genes). So each published set was correlated against NDRG1 over `curated ∩ published`: 11 of 49 readable members for the Buffa metagene, 18 of 188 for pparg_chip_chea. About a tenth of each panel, under the panel's name. ⭐ No new MSigDB fetch and no wider accession bridge are needed — the bridge is platform-wide and already built.
what_shipped: The generator now emits `signature_member_reads`: per-sample within-array z for every readable member of every RESOLVED set, sample order stated once per matrix and each gene a positional array of z alone. The attribution reads it, merges it under `gene_reads` (which wins on a gene in both, so a widened run cannot silently move a published number), and — the part that decides the verdict — DRAWS THE SIZE-MATCHED NULL FROM THE WIDENED POOL.
the_size_decision: ⭐ MEASURED BEFORE CHOOSING, NOT AFTER. The obvious fix (add the genes to `gene_reads`) costs +13 MB on a 7.4 MB artifact regenerated whole every dispatch, because a record is ~7.2 kB and 81%/67% of it is `per_sample` repeating gsm/class/value as JSON keys per row. Lean records there save only about a fifth — `per_sample` IS the bulk — and buy two shapes in one map. The positional block is ~1.4 MB for the same z values across all 30 sets, perturbs no existing consumer, and stays inside `derive()`, the OFFLINE half, so `--check` still re-derives it.
what_is_NOT_done: ⛔ THE DATA. The sandbox cannot reach GEO (the egress proxy 403s it — the standing reason this workflow mode exists), so the widened numbers do not exist yet. The regenerated attribution artifact is byte-identical in EVERY number and gained only `panel_membership_source`, which reads `gene_reads only` — the narrow read, saying so on its own face. It becomes the wide read on the first `panels` dispatch carrying this generator.
why_that_field_exists: ⛔ THE TWO READS PRODUCE DIFFERENT NUMBERS UNDER THE SAME FIELD NAMES, and the null's pool differs between them, so they are not comparable. A reader who cannot tell which one they are holding has the worse of both. The field is asserted by a test rather than trusted, in both directions.
